notes.title: Oblivion.exe static recon: full RTTI, voice file naming, and game-setting defaults compiled into the exe
notes.game_version: Steam retail build, PE timestamp 0x462392c7 (2007-04-16), Oblivion.esm from the same install, Linux host with Python 3.14
notes.anti_cheat: None involved: files read from disk only; the exe was never run, attached to or patched (a protection stub wraps the entry point)
notes.summary: Static analysis of the retail Steam executable, in support of an OpenMW-based Android port. It has full MSVC RTTI (1,715 vtables, 1,482 classes), the voice file name format is confirmed by the exe itself, and ~2,050 game-setting defaults live in static initializers (so "settings absent from the master" still have values). All results come from read-only scripts that finish in under a second.
notes.verification: Name coverage: the GMST extraction covers 378 of the 382 GMST records in the master. An independent disassembly-based extractor (objdump text, floats only) agreed on all 711 float defaults it produced. Voice naming matches archive contents and the bsa-rs example. CTDA size measured over every condition. **Not verified**: runtime behaviour (the exe was never run), the topic-list rule, the quest-script delay value, struct layouts of the classes.

gotcha_items.symptom: Entry point sits in a high-entropy `.bind` section
gotcha_items.cause: a protection stub wraps the exe.
gotcha_items.fix: analyse only the readable `.text/.rdata/.data`; do not attempt to remove the wrapper; everything above was possible without it.

gotcha_items.symptom: String has no code references
gotcha_items.cause: it is referenced from a data table (command table, setting table).
gotcha_items.fix: treat data xrefs as table entries, compute the record stride from consecutive references, and read the table.

gotcha_items.symptom: Naive GMST scan found only strings
gotcha_items.cause: floats load their default with `fld [addr]; push ecx; fstp [esp]` (an offset arithmetic bug of mine made the scan miss them).
gotcha_items.fix: anchor on `push NAME; mov ecx, OBJ; call` and look back exactly 10 bytes for the float form, 5 bytes for `push imm32`.

gotcha_items.symptom: ~20% of settings still missing
gotcha_items.cause: 0.0 and 1.0 use `fldz`/`fld1`, and for those the compiler puts `mov ecx, OBJ` *before* `push NAME`; small ints use `push imm8`.
gotcha_items.fix: scan both instruction orders and both push forms; coverage went from 285 to 306 to 378 of 382.

gotcha_items.symptom: Most exe defaults differ from the master's values
gotcha_items.cause: the master overrides placeholder defaults (strings like "Need a gamesetting description.").
gotcha_items.fix: do not use equality with the master as the oracle; use name coverage, an independent extractor, and non-trivial equal values.

gotcha_items.symptom: `approx func` from the string tool lands mid-function
gotcha_items.cause: it only looks for the previous padding run.
gotcha_items.fix: treat it as a reading start, confirm with a prologue.

gotcha_items.symptom: Dumps are exe-derived
gotcha_items.fix: keep class maps and setting tables out of public repositories; publish method, counts and rules.
gotcha_items.detail: Fix: keep class maps and setting tables out of public repositories; publish method, counts and rules.

notes.title: Oblivion's UI is data (menu XML in Misc.bsa) and how to measure script-command coverage by call sites
notes.game_version: Steam retail install; Oblivion.esm and Oblivion - Misc.bsa from the same install
notes.anti_cheat: None involved: files read from disk only
notes.summary: Two measurements that change how a port should be planned: the original menus are 104 XML files (an expression language over DDS art), so UI parity means writing an interpreter, not hand-building screens; and counting command call sites in the compiled master shows which subsystems (not which commands) the script runtime is missing.
notes.verification: Counts are exact for the compiled data; the subsystem buckets are regex-based and approximate (about 1,000 sites stayed unbucketed). Not verified: that every menu is expressible by an interpreter of the common tags (a long tail of 500+ tags exists), runtime behaviour of the original menus.

gotcha_items.symptom: Command coverage by distinct names looks small
gotcha_items.cause: the long tail of rare commands.
gotcha_items.fix: weigh by call sites and group by subsystem; five subsystems explain most of the gap.

gotcha_items.symptom: A missing command that returns a value is not a harmless stub
gotcha_items.cause: the runtime returns 0 and logs once, so conditions silently take the wrong branch.
gotcha_items.fix: count value-returning stubs separately and make them loud.

gotcha_items.symptom: Regex bucketing misfiles commands
gotcha_items.fix: treat percentages as approximate; fix the bucket table when reviewing the top 50.
gotcha_items.detail: Fix: treat percentages as approximate; fix the bucket table when reviewing the top 50.

gotcha_items.symptom: Menu XML invites hand-translation
gotcha_items.cause: each screen is small.
gotcha_items.fix: write the expression/tile interpreter once; per-menu code should only supply user-trait values.

gotcha_items.symptom: Setting not found among game settings
gotcha_items.cause: it is an INI setting (name carries a `:Section` suffix in the executable) with its default in the shipped INI file.
gotcha_items.fix: look in `Oblivion_default.ini` and for `name:Section` strings.

notes.title: OpenOblivion movement and collision case study: authored Havok collision, the measured player hull, stair camera timing, gait, silent model failures
notes.game_version: Steam retail Oblivion (exe PE timestamp 0x462392c7 for class facts); owner's Vilverin visual slice for data facts; OpenOblivion preview builds 0.3-0.23 on OpenMW 0.52 (desktop pin) and the Android 0.51 base
tools: desktop probe with a scripted controls driver
read-only process-memory sampler on the owner's own copy
notes.anti_cheat: None involved: owner's own single-player copy, offline; the sampler only read memory of an unchanged copy; nothing written to the process; no DRM or protection touched
agents: Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5), compiled from the OpenOblivion project docs and private metrics
notes.summary: What a patched-donor port learned about Oblivion's Havok-facing movement: collision is authored (and differs from the render mesh), the player is a pointed convex hull and not a capsule, the donor's stair solver breaks when you give it that hull unless you port the support-point ground test, stair camera smoothing must run after physics, and a failed model load can masquerade as a collision bug. Each lesson links an experiment record; reusable physics knowledge is in `bethesda-gamebryo-re/refere
notes.verification: Paired same-binary probes (raw versus changed), gates for walking response, stopping, jump/landing, a wall that must block, healthy-tracking control; ray grids on matching AABBs; the original's own Z(Y) samples; independent decoders for animation; emulator before/after harnesses. **Not verified:** any phone result of the hull, authored-collision or gait builds (phone testing is paused), original step/slope/jump, run speed, anything outside the Vilverin slice, and the isolated cause of the Lua-filter regression.

gotcha_items.symptom: Per-tread camera jolt although the body climbs fine
gotcha_items.cause: the view follows the player root through discrete rises; an eye filter in Lua `onFrame` runs before physics and the camera update at the OpenMW pin and regressed the real ascent (1206.7 to 3008.3) while passing on the synthetic fixture.
gotcha_items.fix: apply the smoothing inside the camera position update after physics (1321.4 to 535.7). The phase explanation is inferred, not isolated (EXP-OO-001, EXP-OO-002).

gotcha_items.symptom: A change looked good on the generated stair fixture and bad on the real stairs
gotcha_items.cause: not established; the synthetic route is a clean staircase and the real treads are irregular, and the Lua filter's result differed even between real ascent (worse) and real descent (better).
gotcha_items.fix: require a real-stair route in every paired probe and keep the fixture as a first oracle only (EXP-OO-001).

gotcha_items.symptom: Collision came out seven times too large
gotcha_items.cause: the packed-vertex factor of 7 was applied to `bhkNiTriStripsShape` vertices that are already in mesh units.
gotcha_items.fix: choose the scale per shape class and compare bounds first (EXP-OO-004).

gotcha_items.symptom: Player climbed at 440 to 480 units/s after swapping in the measured hull
gotcha_items.cause: the cone's contact on a tread edge failed the donor's walkable-normal test, so the inherited stair hack moved the body 10 units per frame.
gotcha_items.fix: judge walkability from the support point under the hull centre (EXP-OO-005, EXP-OO-006).

gotcha_items.symptom: Player stopped at a visibly open doorway
gotcha_items.cause: the player collision model failed to load and the engine silently substituted a 123-unit error-marker body (the frame opens 111 units at mid height).
gotcha_items.fix: correct the model file and make a failed supplied model fail the probe; read load errors before debugging collision (EXP-OO-009).

gotcha_items.symptom: Run looked the same as walk; three binding experiments changed nothing
gotcha_items.cause: the donor selects gait from the animation state machine and the preview player had no locomotion animations.
gotcha_items.fix: override the maximum-speed function with the settings-based formula (EXP-OO-007, EXP-OO-008).

gotcha_items.symptom: The port stood about 3.25 units higher than the original on flat floor
gotcha_items.cause: the original hull floats about 4 units above the floor triangles and its reference sits below them; the port rested the hull on the floor.
gotcha_items.fix: not applied; recorded as measured but unreproduced (finding `oblivion-controller-floats-above-floor`).

gotcha_items.symptom: Triangle counts disagree between the file and the loader
gotcha_items.cause: a serialized strip of length n is n-2 triangles, but degenerate strip steps (two equal indices) are dropped (1,288 serialized, 575 kept on one stair).
gotcha_items.fix: count the way the loader builds, and say which you mean.

gotcha_items.symptom: Skeleton loaded, animation clock ran, still a T-pose
gotcha_items.cause: the attachment filter copied each part's private skeleton, so skinned parts bound to bones that were not animated; separately the donor looked bones up by Morrowind names that Oblivion's skeleton lacks.
gotcha_items.fix: copy the renderable's local subtree so parts resolve the actor's animated bones; list the skeleton's node names before assuming a mapping (EXP-OO-012).

gotcha_items.symptom: The same configuration gave different numbers in different runs
gotcha_items.cause: run-to-run variation in the probe (box-body ascent variation 2,379 versus 2,128; the real-ascent raw baseline 1206.7 in one series and 1321.4 in another).
gotcha_items.fix: compare rows produced by the same binary in the same series, change one thing per experiment, and record the metric's name with every number.

notes.title: OpenOblivion lessons: TES4 script compiler, dialogue/quest runtime, SpeedTree billboards and touch menus on a patched OpenMW
notes.game_version: OpenOblivion builds 0.40-0.44 on a patched OpenMW (desktop pin vs Android donor, Lua API rev 160 vs 129); Oblivion.esm from a retail install
notes.summary: What a 1:1 Android port of Oblivion on a patched OpenMW needed for trees, quests/journal, spoken conversations, object scripts and always-closable menus, with the bugs that cost time. Verified on desktop probes and CI; phone confirmation of 0.40-0.44 was pending when written.
notes.verification: Compiler statement-level opcode sequence equals the bytecode's for all 7,945 scripts with both source and bytecode (two differ: their source lacks an End/Endif); fixtures for compiler, runtime and dialogue run in CTest; end-to-end on the real master with a mock world (starting a new game chains quest stages with journal text); desktop probes screenshot the conversation window and journal. **Not verified**: phone behaviour of 0.40-0.44, voice playback audibility, trunk collision, rule guesses above.

gotcha_items.symptom: Generated Lua was invalid for unclosed or stray `If/Else/Endif`
gotcha_items.cause: scripts whose source lacks an End/Endif.
gotcha_items.fix: stack-guard blocks with `[kind, else_seen]` and close implicitly.

gotcha_items.symptom: Dialogue condition groups misbehaved at the end of a list
gotcha_items.cause: trailing OR.
gotcha_items.fix: an explicit `open` flag on the group.

gotcha_items.symptom: FormIDs did not match across files
gotcha_items.cause: load-order byte in the high byte.
gotcha_items.fix: `% 0x1000000` before comparing.

gotcha_items.symptom: Command parameter types mismatched at compile time
gotcha_items.cause: a second, hand-written table disagreed with the extractor's output.
gotcha_items.fix: use the committed extractor output only.

gotcha_items.symptom: Android build error returning a shared_ptr where an `osg::ref_ptr` was expected
gotcha_items.fix: `return {};` in the patch.

gotcha_items.symptom: Desktop probe lost overlay scripts when positioning the player
gotcha_items.cause: the start-position script teleported.
gotcha_items.fix: skip the teleport when a start-override module is present.

gotcha_items.symptom: Probe screenshots taken before the UI existed
gotcha_items.fix: guard on `not config.ui` timing.

gotcha_items.symptom: xdotool clicks failed in the probe container
gotcha_items.cause: missing `XAUTHORITY`.
gotcha_items.fix: set it; poll container logs instead of waiting for a stdout file written at the end.

gotcha_items.symptom: Phone user could not close the journal
gotcha_items.cause: unconfirmed (22 px "Close" text easy to miss on touch).
gotcha_items.fix: BACK button in the touch overlay while any menu is open (sends Escape), Android back key closes menus first, big Close/Goodbye buttons, tap on any unused part of the page closes it, and `OPENOBLIVION_UI tap` logging to separate "tap never arrived" from "tap did nothing".

gotcha_items.symptom: A patch script clobbered pristine copies
gotcha_items.fix: generate patches from `trees/KIND/a` copies, never overwrite the pristines.
gotcha_items.detail: Fix: generate patches from `trees/KIND/a` copies, never overwrite the pristines.

gotcha_items.symptom: Trees invisible
gotcha_items.cause: OpenMW ignores `.spt` SpeedTree files.
gotcha_items.fix: a `tes4_trees` receipt turns `.spt` into two crossed billboard quads sized from the TREE record's billboard width/height, with `simpleLighting`; pitfall: `SceneUtil::Material` versus `osg::Material` differ between pins.

notes.title: Driving an Android phone with adb from a remote build host over Tailscale (Termux self-pair, adb tcpip)
notes.summary: No USB cable and no shared Wi-Fi needed: pair the phone with itself in Termux, switch its adbd to TCP 5555, and `adb connect` to the phone's Tailscale address from the build host. Measured on a Galaxy S24+ (Android 16): 23 ms round trip on a direct tailnet path, about 6 MB/s for a 292 MB `adb install`.
notes.verification: Worked end to end in one session: connect, `adb install -r` of a 292 MB APK, launching, `screencap`, `logcat`, `input tap` and `input keyevent`, `run-as` on a debuggable build. Not verified: how long `tcpip` mode survives a Wi-Fi change (expect it to end), other Android versions or OEM skins, running without Termux (for example Shizuku).

gotcha_items.symptom: `failed to authenticate` / `unauthorized` right after `adb connect`
gotcha_items.cause: the phone's key prompt is waiting.
gotcha_items.fix: accept the prompt on the phone, then run `adb connect` again.

gotcha_items.symptom: `adb pair` is refused or times out
gotcha_items.cause: the pairing code or port changed (they are single use and expire when the dialog closes).
gotcha_items.fix: reopen "Pair device with pairing code" and use the new values; pairing and connect use different ports.

gotcha_items.symptom: Connection drops after a reboot or Wi-Fi switch
gotcha_items.cause: `adb tcpip` is not persistent.
gotcha_items.fix: repeat step 3 (the owner must do it; the agent cannot).

gotcha_items.symptom: A bare `adb install` goes to the wrong device
gotcha_items.cause: with one device attached adb picks it silently, and the phone may be that device.
gotcha_items.fix: always pass `-s`; when the owner pauses phone testing, run `adb disconnect` at once.

gotcha_items.symptom: A lock screen blocks input tests
gotcha_items.cause: `input` events do not unlock.
gotcha_items.fix: ask the owner to set a long screen timeout for the test session, or to unlock; never store a PIN they share in notes or files, and suggest they change it afterwards.

gotcha_items.symptom: Android 16 shows two dialogs on launch of a sideloaded build
gotcha_items.cause: a debuggable APK and native libraries that are not 16 KB aligned.
gotcha_items.fix: informational; ship a release-style build with 16 KB-aligned libraries to remove them.

notes.title: Testing arm64-only Android native ports on an x86_64 emulator: GLES translation crash, native x86_64 rebuild, GL4ES/EGL start-up deadlock
notes.summary: If an Android port ships only arm64 libraries and renders through GL4ES/GLES, the stock x86_64 emulator crashes in Google's ARM translation layer. Build the same source for x86_64, add `lib/x86_64` to a copy of the APK, and drive it with a scripted adb gate. Doing this also exposed a real start-up deadlock between GL4ES's load-time `eglGetDisplay` and the UI RenderThread.
notes.verification: Measured on an Android 16 (API 36) google_apis x86_64 emulator with host GPU: arm64 build crashed at scene start on Android 14 and 16, host GPU and software; x86_64 build starts, renders and passes a six-check gate (launcher ready, engine thread started, 20 s stable, drawn frame, menu opens, system BACK closes it). Start-up deadlock: 3 of 4 launches hung before the fix, 5 of 5 started after it (small sample). Not verified: the deadlock on real phones (EGL starts faster there; the race is plausible but unobserved), any arm64-specific behaviour, performance.

gotcha_items.symptom: SIGSEGV at scene start, fault address 0, frame in `libndk_translation_proxy_libGLESv2.so` (Android 14) or `berberis::TrampolineFuncGenerator<unsigned int ()>` (Android 16)
gotcha_items.cause: the translation layer's GLES proxy exposes entry points the emulator's GPU library does not implement, so a call target is null; GL4ES reaches it during init. Host GPU vs software rendering makes no difference, and a newer image did not fix it.
gotcha_items.fix: do not chase the function; run a native x86_64 build.

gotcha_items.symptom: Process alive, 0% CPU, window list shows only the system "Splash Screen", log stops right after the activity's `onCreate`, "Launch timeout has expired"
gotcha_items.cause: lock-order deadlock. The main thread is inside `dlopen` of the GL4ES library (linker lock held) whose constructor calls `eglGetDisplay`, which waits for libEGL's driver-init mutex; the UI RenderThread holds that mutex while loading the driver and needs the linker lock (`dlsym`). Slow emulator EGL start makes it likely.
gotcha_items.fix: call `EGL14.eglGetDisplay(EGL_DEFAULT_DISPLAY)` on the main thread before the first `System.loadLibrary`.

gotcha_items.symptom: `configure: error: no nasm` building libjpeg-turbo for x86_64
gotcha_items.cause: SIMD needs NASM and the host has none.
gotcha_items.fix: configure `--without-simd` (slower JPEG decode, nothing else changes) or install nasm.

gotcha_items.symptom: FFmpeg configure: `unknown target CPU 'intel'`, "C compiler test failed"
gotcha_items.cause: an old `-march=intel` in the donor script.

gotcha_items.symptom: System BACK key does nothing in an SDL activity
gotcha_items.cause: SDLActivity forwards the key to the engine and consumes it, so `onBackPressed` never runs.
gotcha_items.fix: override `dispatchKeyEvent`, handle `KEYCODE_BACK` on ACTION_DOWN, consume the matching ACTION_UP, otherwise call super.

gotcha_items.symptom: First launch shows a "Viewing full screen" dialog that holds window focus
gotcha_items.cause: Android's one-time immersive-mode notice.
gotcha_items.fix: tap "Got it" (found with `uiautomator dump`); it does not return after confirmation.

gotcha_items.symptom: Reinstall wipes a large data payload
gotcha_items.cause: `adb install -r` over a build signed with a different key fails, and uninstall deletes app data.
gotcha_items.fix: always sign emulator APKs with the same debug key so `-r` keeps the extracted payload.

gotcha_items.symptom: Scripts reach the wrong device
gotcha_items.cause: a bare `adb` command uses the only connected device, which may be the owner's phone.
gotcha_items.fix: always `-s SERIAL`, disconnect phones, and make the script refuse non-`emulator-` serials by default.

gotcha_items.symptom: Shell helper breaks under zsh
gotcha_items.cause: `E="adb -s emu"; $E shell ...` is not word-split in zsh, and `pgrep -f` matches the shell's own command line.
gotcha_items.fix: use a function (`a() { adb -s emu "$@"; }`) and check logs or `pidof` instead of `pgrep -f`.

notes.title: Measuring an original game's character controller by replaying its own timesteps (live read-only sampler + per-update replay oracle)
notes.summary: Sample the running original at several times its update rate, collapse the samples into the game's own updates, then replay a candidate law over each update using the `dt` the game logged. If the law is right the residual is zero to rounding. It turned three guesses about Oblivion's jump (height, takeoff speed, integration order) and two about air control into exact statements with an hour of work, and it explained why every apex we had measured before disagreed with the formula.
notes.verification: Replay residuals are exact on the recorded traces. The support range (2.0 Havok units), the level-ground hover and the capture rule replay at 21 and 30 updates/s (EXP-OO-018). Not verified: other Acrobatics values (the player's was 5), 60 fps, encumbrance, fatigue cost, creatures and NPCs, swimming, walkable slopes, and the classification that makes stair contacts accumulate velocity (EXP-OO-019).

gotcha_items.symptom: Reading another process's memory is refused even for your own user
gotcha_items.detail: (Yama `ptrace_scope` 1) when the game is not a descendant of the sampler. Run the read-only sampler with the privileges your system needs, guard it with a check that the target's command line is the isolated reference, and never write.

gotcha_items.symptom: The first jump trial reads a lower apex than the formula
gotcha_items.detail: if there is a ceiling (the start corridor capped a jump at 32 units). Choose open space and look at `z` against a known ceiling before trusting an apex.

gotcha_items.symptom: A held jump or any wall-clock comparison hides the cause
gotcha_items.detail: : compare per update with the logged `dt`.

gotcha_items.symptom: Console toggling needs a held key
gotcha_items.detail: A 28 fps game can miss a press shorter than a frame; send key down, wait 0.15 s, key up. Typed text is lost if the console is still closed (the letters become game input).

gotcha_items.symptom: `pkill -f '<pattern>'` kills the shell that contains the pattern
gotcha_items.detail: (and the tool call with it). Use `pgrep -f '[Z]:.*Oblivion.exe'` style patterns.

gotcha_items.symptom: Teleporting twice in a row once ended in the main menu
gotcha_items.detail: (probably a death and reload); relaunch and walk instead of chaining `setpos`.

gotcha_items.symptom: A port's own bookkeeping can break at a higher frame rate than the one you tested
gotcha_items.detail: Add a one-line log of the quantity you matched (here each jump's rise) so the device reports it; the first phone run showed `rise 0` where the desktop showed 66.8 (EXP-OO-017).

gotcha_items.symptom: Placement trials (`player.setpos z`) find ranges that a walk cannot
gotcha_items.detail: Put the player N units above a flat floor for several N, bracket the switch point with 0.2 to 0.5 unit steps, and read the first update's state. A drop of about 125 units kills the level-1 player and the game falls back to the main menu: restore health between drops, or the next typed commands go i…

gotcha_items.symptom: The port's own physics step is not constant either
gotcha_items.detail: The first steps after a cell loads carried 0.2, 0.07 and 0.02 s; a position-based test started at load measures the hitch, not the law. Start such tests from a jump (or after a settle) and pass the recorded next step into any function that prepares a velocity for the following update.

gotcha_items.symptom: Software GL cannot give a high frame rate on an exterior cell
gotcha_items.detail: (10 to 13 updates/s even at 320x240 with grass and water effects off). Laws that depend on `dt` squared (a hover) need an interior at 30 Hz or hardware GL to be seen on slopes.

notes.title: Reviewing an in-flight game port: what to measure first (feedback loop, engine split, subsystem ceiling, UI as data, documentation drift)
notes.summary: A week-old, fast-moving port (OpenMW-based reimplementation of a 2006 RPG for Android) had good evidence discipline and still stalled on five structural problems. Each had a cheap measurement that turned an opinion into a number. Use the list on any port or decomp that has outgrown its first plan.
notes.verification: Every number above was measured from the repository, the packaged APK and the owner's local data on 2026-10-06 and is recorded with sources in the project's review document. Judgement calls (which phase first) are labelled as such there. Not verified: that the proposed phases fit the effort estimates.

gotcha_items.symptom: A "new finding" that the repository already contains
gotcha_items.cause: claiming a result (here: that game-setting defaults would settle movement speed) without searching the project's own docs first. The formula had been decoded earlier.
gotcha_items.fix: grep the repository's research notes for the topic before writing a finding; correct the claim everywhere it was repeated (docs, skill text, memory) as soon as it is wrong.

gotcha_items.symptom: Counting commands instead of call sites
gotcha_items.cause: a flat count treats a command used once like one used 3,000 times.
gotcha_items.fix: weight by occurrences in the real corpus.

gotcha_items.symptom: Running tests the wrong way
gotcha_items.cause: the project's test scripts take CMake-style arguments (the repository root); bare invocations fail with confusing errors.
gotcha_items.fix: read how CI invokes them and copy that.

gotcha_items.symptom: A tool that quietly overwrites repository edits
gotcha_items.cause: a publish script copied files out of an installed location into the repository.
gotcha_items.fix: make the repository the source of truth and copy outward only.

gotcha_items.symptom: Search that returns plausible but irrelevant notes
gotcha_items.cause: BM25 on short queries matches common words.
gotcha_items.fix: stopwords for filler terms and a minimum share of query terms matched.

notes.title: Static recon of MSVC game executables in pure Python: PE triage, RTTI classes, string pivots, signatures
notes.summary: Four dependency-free scripts that triage a PE, recover C++ class names and inheritance from MSVC RTTI, find the code that references a string, and build version-robust byte signatures. Verified on x86 (Oblivion.exe, GoldSrc engine DLL) and x64 (a Unity player DLL, Unreal executables) binaries.
notes.verification: Cross-checks: RTTI base lists agree with known hierarchies; string xrefs resolve to plausible functions; signatures are unique on the build they came from. Timings: 0.08-0.28 s per binary for RTTI. Not verified: Windows paths, 32-bit-only edge cases like MI with virtual bases, binaries with stripped or `/GR-` builds (they simply return nothing).

gotcha_items.symptom: No RTTI found
gotcha_items.cause: `/GR-`, stripped, or non-MSVC (GCC uses a different RTTI).
gotcha_items.fix: say so; fall back to strings and constructors.

gotcha_items.symptom: x86 locator scan matches garbage
gotcha_items.cause: a dword equal to a descriptor VA by chance.
gotcha_items.fix: require signature 0, small offset fields, a class-hierarchy pointer inside the image, and a vftable reference.

gotcha_items.symptom: Pointer-heuristic false positives in signatures
gotcha_items.cause: immediates that resemble in-image pointers.
gotcha_items.fix: harmless for uniqueness (they only widen wildcards), but re-test uniqueness with `find`.

gotcha_items.symptom: Function start guessed wrong
gotcha_items.cause: padding-run heuristic.
gotcha_items.fix: confirm a prologue (`55 8B EC`, `6A FF` for SEH) or use a disassembler's function boundary.

gotcha_items.symptom: Rich header product ids look unfamiliar
gotcha_items.cause: id tables are long and version-specific.
gotcha_items.fix: rely on the build number (e.g. 8168 = VC6 RTM, 3077 = 7.1, 50727 = VS2005) and confirm against the project's compiler.

gotcha_items.symptom: Wrapped executables
gotcha_items.cause: protection stub with a high-entropy entry section.
gotcha_items.fix: analyse only the readable sections; never attempt removal.
